description: Scheduled Tasks page — manages recurring task execution. A task pairs an arbitrary task type (Workflow / Prompt / Auto-Fix / Watcher / Background-capture / Remote agent) with a schedule (cron / interval / once / condition). The page surfaces the task list, execution history with launch-failure and missed-runner-down indicators, and scheduler engine settings, plus a New Task form covering all variants and catch-up policy.

groups.description: When a runner is offline at a task's scheduled fire time, the catch-up reconciler decides what to do. Users select per-task behavior via the 'If the runner was down' selector, with three options that map to the runner's CatchUpPolicy enum: 'run_once' (default — collapse all missed slots into one execution after the runner returns), 'run' (execute each missed slot individually), and 'skip' (record each missed slot as MissedRunnerDown without executing). A 'Grace window' input sets the seconds of slack — slots within `now - grace` of restart are considered fresh and not eligible for catch-up. The selector is only relevant for time-based schedules (Cron / Once / Interval); condition-based schedules don't have missed slots.
groups.name: Catch-up Policy Controls (Phase A/B/E)

groups.description: The 'Remote agent' task type lets users schedule arbitrary Claude prompts without pre-registering them in the prompt library. When this radio is selected the form reveals a multi-line prompt textarea, optional working directory, model selector, allowed-tools chip group, and an Advanced disclosure containing max-turns, timeout, and MCP-connection editor. At dispatch time the runner's launch_remote_agent calls POST /prompts/run with these fields. The form's defaults match the runner-side defaults (model = sonnet-4-6, allowed_tools = Bash/Read/Write/Edit/Glob/Grep, max_turns = 50, timeout = 600s); drift between form defaults and runner defaults causes silent behavior changes.
groups.name: Remote Agent Task Type Form (Phase D/E)

groups.description: When a scheduled task's launch (start call) fails — e.g. workflow file missing, prompt-id not found, /prompts/run HTTP error, missing session_id — the runner increments task.consecutive_launch_failures and pushes next_run forward by min(base * 2^(failures-1), 86400) seconds. The task list surfaces this so the operator can see retries are being throttled. Required visual indicators: an orange 'launch_failed' badge on the task row, the next-run cell rendered as 'Next: in X (after N failures)' instead of plain 'Next: in X', and a tooltip explaining the wait. This is distinct from a runtime failure (status 'failed'), which doesn't push next_run forward — backoff applies only to LaunchFailed.
groups.name: Launch Failure Backoff Display in Task List (Phase C/E)

groups.description: The History sub-tab shows one row per execution. Beyond the original Pending/Running/Completed/Failed/Skipped/Cancelled, two new statuses landed in Phase B: 'launch_failed' (LaunchFailed — task could not start) and 'missed_runner_down' (MissedRunnerDown — slot was synthesized by the catch-up reconciler with policy=Skip). These need distinguishable visual treatment because they mean different things from generic Failed: launch_failed is retry-with-backoff, missed_runner_down is informational. Catch-up runs also tag the task name with '(catch-up)' so the operator can tell that a Completed row was a catch-up rather than a normal-schedule fire.
groups.name: History Status Badges for New Statuses (Phase B/E)

groups.description: Style-guide coverage: scheduler tab uses the runner's standard panel layout with semantic accent colors for status indicators. Critical theme tokens: orange for transient/retry states (launch_failed, launch-failure backoff badge), slate for neutral/informational (missed_runner_down), red for permanent failures (failed), green for completed, blue for running, yellow for pending/skipped. These accent semantics MUST stay consistent across the task list, history rows, and any new surface that displays task state, otherwise operators will misread severity.
groups.name: Visual Design and Theme Compliance
